description: We are the Planetary Innovation Agency, a team driven by innovation, curiosity, and real-world impact. Climate change and food security are urgent global crises that affect communities everywhere. As shifting weather patterns, severe droughts, and soil degradation threaten crop yields around the world, we are harnessing NASA space data to build smart, adaptable tools that help farmers thrive. (no need to write 500 word essay  to join . just 3 sentences )
summary: We developed Smart Farm, a smart web app that helps farmers adapt to climate change using NASA satellite data. When a farmer clicks their land on our map, the app checks local soil moisture, heat, and rainfall trends. It gives their current crop a simple survival score and suggests tougher alternative crops and rotation plans if the climate has shifted. This protects harvests and global food supplies and our scoring engine even expands to evaluate future farming sites on Mars and the Moon.
details:
This project was coded with the assistance of AI tools, allowing our team to rapidly prototype, test, and connect complex NASA datasets into a working web application.

What It Does and How It Works
Smart Farm is an interactive web dashboard that helps farmers decide what to plant, where to plant it, and when to pivot as local climates change. Users select a catchment area or farm on a live satellite map, view NASA cropland and vegetation health overlays, and choose their current crop. Behind the scenes, our app fetches real-time temperature, rainfall, and root-zone soil moisture data from NASA satellites. It runs these measurements through a transparent Weighted Suitability Index formula, comparing live conditions against ideal crop ranges to generate a 0–100% survival score. If a crop is at risk, the app recommends resilient alternatives and a two-season crop rotation plan.

Benefits and Intended Impact
Complex satellite data is often too technical for everyday farmers to use. Our app translates raw orbital measurements into plain-language verdicts, helping farmers avoid failed harvests, protect soil health, and conserve water. We also included a low-data SMS alert feature so farmers in rural areas with limited internet access can still receive critical planting advice, supporting global food security.

Tools, Software, and Data Used

  • Development Tools: Google AI Studio, React, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, and Leaflet for interactive mapping.
  • NASA Datasets & APIs: NASA POWER API (temperature, precipitation, and root-zone soil wetness), NASA GIBS (MODIS vegetation health and GFSAD global cropland overlays), and NASA Trek orbital maps (Mars MOLA/SHARAD and Lunar LRO).
  • Supporting Data: FAO EcoCrop agricultural standards and OpenStreetMap APIs for location search and local farm boundaries.

Creativity and Key Factors Considered
Our team focused on accessibility, explainability, and future scalability. Rather than using a confusing "black-box" model, we built a transparent scoring engine so farmers understand exactly why a crop is struggling. Finally, because our scoring math is built on universal physical variables like water, temperature, and terrain we creatively added a Planetary Mode. This lets users toggle from Earth to Mars (Arcadia Planitia) and the Moon (Shackleton Crater Rim) to identify safe landing zones near subsurface water ice for future space agriculture.
